objective: Issue #6: compare at least three existing alternatives and test whether an unmet small-subcontractor export gap is supported.
summary: Compared LCPcertified, Sunburst CPS and Payroll4Construction across four public vendor documents. All advertise reporting workflows; Sunburst also documents a Desktop-only boundary and linked-record configuration. This narrows the research toward specific interoperability exceptions, but no independent small-contractor evidence establishes residual pain. Pause generic form-generation exploration; do not create an opportunity record.
questions: What source data and output paths do existing products advertise?
What is the difference between additional configuration and a demonstrated unresolved problem?
Is there independent first-hand evidence of an economically meaningful exception?

findings.text: LCPcertified: payroll-data upload → validation/mathematical checks → certified reports, with XML outputs listed for California, Washington and Maryland. The public page does not establish every supported payroll version or field mapping.

Sunburst CPS: QuickBooks Desktop employee/job/time/payroll data + additional linked employee/job/wage/deduction records → federal/state and named electronic reporting outputs. Linked records are a setup/input requirement, not evidence of recurrent failure.

Payroll4Construction: submitted timecards → managed construction payroll and QuickBooks accounting integration → automatically generated print/electronic certified reports. It is a service/switching alternative, not a demonstrated drop-in transformation layer for any incumbent stack.
Sunburst says its products do not support QBO. The older vendor explanation is not verified against current Intuit APIs and must not be generalized to a market-wide impossibility.
The current evidence favors narrowing to a payroll-stack/destination-portal pair rather than a broad certified-form generator. This is a research priority judgment, not customer validation.

contradictory_findings.text: Advertised upload, merging, automatic generation and named electronic outputs provide concrete alternatives to manual report production. They weaken the assumption that required weekly work is itself an unmet software need.
A platform-specific limitation at one vendor does not establish that all competing vendors or QBO itself leave the workflow unsolved.

unresolved_questions: No dated independent small-contractor account of a residual export failure was obtained in this bounded search. Do not present marketing copy or curated testimonials as that evidence.

The search attempted Google (JavaScript-only response), Bing (irrelevant results), DuckDuckGo (human challenge; not attempted) and a public Intuit community search route (404). These outcomes establish retrieval limits, not absence of customer pain.
Four source pages are from three suppliers; two Sunburst pages are one interested evidence stream.
No software was installed; no payroll data, pricing comparison, measured avoidable hours, customer budget or willingness to pay were collected.
Original publication dates are unknown; visible Sunburst update dates are recorded as limitations and do not verify present-day compatibility.
conclusions: Complete the bounded documentation comparison, but not the customer-gap investigation. Pause the generic report-generation thesis. A narrow interoperability/exception hypothesis is still unproven and should not be promoted to an opportunity. A future session should first verify official field requirements and find independent contractor evidence, or archive this line if incumbents adequately serve it.
next_steps: Select one source payroll stack and one destination portal; verify current export/import documentation and incumbent coverage before further expansion.
Search for first-hand, dated small-contractor exception accounts; do not contact customers without founder approval.
Revisit only if a reproducible unserved transformation and recurring economically meaningful burden can be evidenced.
title: Certified-payroll alternatives: reporting is served; residual gaps remain unproven

history.reason: Issue #6 public-documentation comparison; no product testing, customer interviews or market validation.
